mainTopic: A נזיר who vows in a בית הקברות: does the vow take effect, does he get מלקות, and must he linger there to be lashed?
overview: This amud continues the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about someone who takes a נזירות vow while standing in a cemetery. ריש לקיש first deflects a challenge by saying the source is about someone who left and came back in. רבי יוחנן then brings a ברייתא showing that the vow of an impure person does take effect. Because of this, מר בר רב אשי recasts the argument. Both agree the vow takes effect, and they only argue about whether he gets מלקות. רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש with inferences from the משנה and a ברייתא, and the גמרא answers both. Finally, an explicit ברייתא says such a person receives forty lashes, and ריש לקיש is refuted (תיובתא). רבא then asks whether he must linger in the cemetery before he is lashed. The גמרא starts working out what case רבא could mean, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the case is one who left and came back in
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers the earlier challenge by saying the source is talking about someone who left the cemetery, became pure, and then came back in.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Someone who went out of the cemetery and then came back in.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends his view, that a vow made in a cemetery does not take effect, by narrowing the case of the earlier source. In that case the person left the cemetery and later re-entered it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source said this person gets מלקות, which sounded like the vow took effect. ריש לקיש says the source means a person who left, purified himself, vowed again, and then went back in. In that situation the נזירות clearly took effect while he was pure, so the lashes do not disprove ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here, with what are we dealing?' The גמרא is about to limit a source to a specific case.
One who left and then entered again.
A cemetery, a place that makes a person impure from the dead.

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
With one who left and entered.
phrases.notes: He means: he left the cemetery, became pure, and was a real נזיר, and only then walked back in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge from the previous section of the daf.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source seemed to give lashes to someone who vowed inside the cemetery, which would mean his vow took effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source is about someone who left, became a pure נזיר, and re-entered, so it says nothing about a vow made while inside.

steps.title: Challenge from the seventh day of an impure person who vowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא that counts the seventh day for an impure person who vowed, which suggests his vow already took effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: The only difference between an impure person who vowed נזירות and a pure נזיר who became impure is this. For the impure person who vowed, his seventh day counts toward his days of נזירות. For the pure נזיר who became impure, his seventh day does not count. If you think the vow of an impure person does not take effect, why does his seventh day count?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש with a ברייתא. It treats the vow of an impure person as already in force, since his seventh day of purification already counts as a day of נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vow did not take effect while he was impure, he should have to vow again after becoming pure, and his count could not already be running on the seventh day. The ברייתא assumes his נזירות is active without a new vow. That contradicts ריש לקיש's claim that it does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: An impure person who took a vow of נזירות.
The seventh day of purification from impurity of the dead.
It counts toward his tally of נזירות days.
If it enters your mind, meaning 'if you were to think...'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people. The one who was impure before vowing gets the seventh day counted. The נזיר who became impure in the middle does not.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him: There is no difference between an impure person who vowed
phrases.notes: The one objecting is רבי יוחנן, still pushing against ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: and a pure nazir who became impure,
except that an impure person who vowed —
his seventh day counts for him toward the tally,
phrases.notes: The seventh day of purifying from impurity of the dead, the day he finishes becoming pure.

phrases.english: while a pure nazir who became impure —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁלּוֹ עוֹלֶה לוֹ לַמִּנְיָן.
phrases.english: his seventh day does not count for him toward the tally.
And if it enters your mind that it does not take effect,
why does it count for him toward the tally?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: אֵין בֵּין טָמֵא שֶׁנָּזַר לְנָזִיר טָהוֹר שֶׁנִּטְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ריש לקיש's answer, רבי יוחנן brings a new and stronger source against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that a vow of נזירות made while impure does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא counts the impure vower's seventh day with no new vow, so his נזירות must already be in force.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: everyone agrees it takes effect, they argue about lashes
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי recasts the argument. Both agree the vow takes effect, and they only disagree about whether he gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: About whether the vow takes effect, everyone agrees that it does. Where they argue is about lashes. רבי יוחנן holds that since it takes effect, he gets lashes. ריש לקיש holds that he does not get lashes, even though it does take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the challenge from the ברייתא, מר בר רב אשי says the argument was never about חלות. It was only about מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both sides fit the ברייתא, since both agree the vow takes effect. The new disagreement is narrower. רבי יוחנן says that once the vow is in force, staying impure earns lashes. ריש לקיש says the vow is in force but brings no lashes in this situation.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking effect.
Everyone agrees, literally 'the whole world does not disagree'.
To be lashed / he is lashed (מלקות).

steps.whyThisMatters: The core category stays the same: he is a real נזיר. The argument moves to one specific result, punishment by lashes.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: מֵיחָל — כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּחָיְילָא,
phrases.english: Regarding taking effect — everyone agrees that it takes effect,
rather, where they disagree is regarding lashes:
Rabbi Yochanan holds:
since it takes effect — he is lashed.
And Reish Lakish holds:
he is not lashed, yet it takes effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: מֵיחָל כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּחָיְילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא by redefining what the argument is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the argument (a different version of the dispute)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought ריש לקיש held the vow does not take effect at all, which the ברייתא contradicts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree the vow takes effect. They argue only about מלקות, so the ברייתא is no problem for either side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: takes effect and he is lashed. ריש לקיש: takes effect but no lashes.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: only the impurity offering is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the משנה as exempting only the קרבן טומאה, which implies lashes still apply. That goes against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: Someone who vowed נזירות while in a cemetery, even if he stayed there thirty days, those days do not count toward his tally, and he does not bring an impurity offering. It is only the impurity offering that he does not bring. So lashes, he does get for it!
steps.whatsHappening: Even under the new version of the argument, רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש. He uses a careful reading of what the משנה leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists what he is exempt from: the days do not count, and he brings no קרבן טומאה. It does not say he is exempt from lashes. רבי יוחנן infers that lashes still apply, which contradicts ריש לקיש's view that he is not lashed.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering a נזיר brings when he becomes impure from the dead.
Thirty days, the standard length of נזירות.
'But this implies...', used to introduce an inference from what the text leaves out.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
One who vowed naziriteship while he was in a cemetery,
even if he was there thirty days —
they do not count for him toward the tally,
and he does not bring an impurity offering.
It is the impurity offering that he does not bring,
but being lashed — he is lashed for it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's position as recast by מר בר רב אשי in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view (in מר בר רב אשי's version) that the vow takes effect but there are no lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה exempts him only from the קרבן טומאה and is silent about lashes, which implies he is lashed.

steps.title: The משנה's wording only matches the next clause
steps.stepSummary: The answer for ריש לקיש is that the משנה really should have said 'he is not flogged.' It said 'he does not bring a קרבן טומאה' only to match the wording of the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: By right, the משנה should have said 'he is not flogged.' But because it wanted to teach in the second part, 'if he left and came back in, the days count and he brings a קרבן טומאה,' it used matching wording in the first part: 'he does not bring a קרבן טומאה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי יוחנן's challenge from step 4 on behalf of ריש לקיש. The משנה's wording does not prove that lashes apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן had argued that since the משנה only exempts the קרבן טומאה, lashes must still apply. The answer is that the משנה picked the phrase 'does not bring a קרבן טומאה' only to parallel the סיפא. The real point is that he is not flogged.

keyTerms.meaning: By right; really it should have been
The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The latter clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The offerings a נזיר brings after becoming impure
Is flogged, receives lashes

phrases.english: By right it should have taught "he is not flogged,"
but because it wants
to teach the latter clause:
"If he left and entered again,
it counts toward his tally,
and he brings the impurity offering,"
it taught in the first clause
"he does not bring the impurity offering."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism: the wording of the רישא was chosen to mirror the סיפא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה exempts only the קרבן טומאה, so lashes still apply
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה really means he is not flogged, and the phrasing just parallels the סיפא

steps.title: A ברייתא lists only one difference, implying both get lashes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the only difference between a טמא שנזר and a נזיר טהור שנטמא is whether the seventh day counts. That implies they are equal regarding מלקות, which goes against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The only difference between an impure person who vowed נזירות and a pure נזיר who became impure is this. For the one who was impure when he vowed, his seventh day counts toward his נזירות. For the pure נזיר who became impure, his seventh day does not count. So regarding lashes, they must be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא is brought to challenge ריש לקיש. If the seventh day is the only difference, then both must get lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'the only difference is...' The inference is that every other law, including מלקות, is the same for both. Everyone agrees a נזיר טהור שנטמא gets lashes, so the טמא שנזר must get them too.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no difference between... (lists the only difference)
The seventh day of purification from טומאת מת
The tally, the count of the נזירות days
Lashes, flogging

phrases.english: Come and hear:
There is no difference between an impure person who vowed נזירות
and a pure נזיר who became impure,
except that for an impure person who vowed,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁלּוֹ עוֹלֶה לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן,
phrases.english: his seventh day counts toward his tally,
and for a pure נזיר who became impure,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁלּוֹ עוֹלֶה לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן.
phrases.english: his seventh day does not count toward his tally.
But regarding lashes, this one and that one are equal!
phrases.notes: This line is the גמרא's own inference from the ברייתא, not part of the ברייתא itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵין בֵּין טָמֵא שֶׁנָּזַר לְנָזִיר טָהוֹר שֶׁנִּטְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 5 defended ריש לקיש, a new source is brought against him
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view (per מר בר רב אשי) that a טמא שנזר is not flogged
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists only one difference, so all other laws, including מלקות, must be the same

steps.title: They are equal in shaving, not in lashes
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the ברייתא's point of equality is shaving. Both must shave on the seventh day. It says nothing about lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. The point is that in shaving, this one and that one are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back. The ברייתא's implied equality is about shaving, not lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש limits what the ברייתא is comparing. The equality it implies is that both must do the purification shaving on the seventh day. So no conclusion about מלקות can be drawn.

keyTerms.meaning: Shaving, here the shaving on the day of purification
This one and that one are equal

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is answering רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: regarding shaving, this one and that one are equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, לְתִגְלַחַת זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the inference to a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא implies they are equal regarding מלקות
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא implies they are equal regarding shaving

steps.title: Then the ברייתא should have listed lashes as a difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses ריש לקיש. If they differ in lashes, the ברייתא should have listed that as a second difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: But regarding lashes, what is the law? This one is flogged and that one is not? Then let the ברייתא teach that difference too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's answer. A ברייתא that says 'the only difference' should not leave out a difference in lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, there are two differences: the seventh day and lashes. But the ברייתא claims there is only one. That seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding, with respect to
Let it teach it! (it should have been stated)

phrases.english: But regarding lashes, what is the law?
This one is flogged and that one is not flogged?
Then let it teach it!

steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the two cases differ regarding מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא that says 'there is no difference except' would have listed a difference in lashes

steps.title: The ברייתא lists only remedies, not punishments
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא only discusses how the נזיר fixes his situation, such as counting days. It does not discuss things that hurt him, like lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is talking about how he fixes his situation. It is not talking about things that are bad for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for ריש לקיש. The ברייתא's list was never meant to include punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'only difference' in the ברייתא is limited to one topic: how the נזיר gets back on track. Lashes are a punishment, so they fall outside that topic. Leaving them out proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: His remedy, how he fixes his situation
His damage, what is bad for him (a punishment)
It is speaking about, dealing with

phrases.english: It is speaking about his remedy;
it is not speaking about what is detrimental to him.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists every difference between the two cases
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא lists only differences about his remedy, not punishments

steps.title: A ברייתא says outright he gets forty lashes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says openly that a טמא שנזר who shaves, drinks wine or becomes impure from a dead body gets the forty lashes. This contradicts ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Someone who was impure and took a נזירות vow may not shave or drink wine. If he shaved, drank wine, or became impure from the dead, he receives the forty lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third source. This one directly says that a טמא שנזר is flogged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no inference to argue about. The ברייתא openly says a person who was impure when he vowed gets מלקות for breaking his נזירות. That flatly contradicts ריש לקיש in מר בר רב אשי's version.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden to shave
Became impure from a dead body
Receives the forty lashes

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁהָיָה טָמֵא וְנָזַר —
phrases.english: Come and hear: One who was impure and vowed נזירות
is forbidden to shave and to drink wine,
and if he shaved, or drank wine,
or became impure from the dead,
he receives the forty lashes!
phrases.notes: 'The forty' is the standard term for Torah lashes, which in practice are 39.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁהָיָה טָמֵא וְנָזַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 deflected the previous source, an explicit source is brought
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view (per מר בר רב אשי) that a טמא שנזר is not flogged
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא rules that a טמא שנזר receives forty lashes

steps.title: ריש לקיש's view is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that ריש לקיש's view, in מר בר רב אשי's version, is refuted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that the last ברייתא decisively disproves ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer can be given for the explicit ברייתא. So in מר בר רב אשי's version of the מחלוקת, ריש לקיש's view that there are no lashes is rejected, and a טמא שנזר is flogged.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation

steps.whatToRemember: In מר בר רב אשי's version, everyone agrees a טמא's vow of נזירות takes effect. ריש לקיש's claim that he gets no מלקות is refuted by an explicit ברייתא: he receives forty lashes.
steps.confusionAlert: The refutation is of ריש לקיש in מר בר רב אשי's version, where the only question is lashes. The earlier version, that the vow does not take effect at all, already ran into the challenge in step 2. That challenge is what led מר בר רב אשי to recast the argument.

phrases.english: This is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes from the קשיא of step 10 that ריש לקיש is refuted
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש's position (per מר בר רב אשי) is refuted. A טמא שנזר who violates his נזירות receives מלקות.

steps.title: רבא asks whether lingering is needed for lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a person who becomes a נזיר while standing in a cemetery must stay there for some time before he gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asks: If someone becomes a נזיר while he is in a cemetery, what is the law? Does he need to stay there a while to get lashes, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. A person took a נזירות vow while standing in a בית הקברות. Does he need to stay there for some time before he deserves lashes?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps decided that such a person gets מלקות. Now רבא asks about timing. Is he punished the moment the vow takes effect, or only after he lingers there, the way someone who becomes טמא in the מקדש is only punished after lingering?

keyTerms.meaning: Asks (a question). In the next phrase the same word means 'needs.'
A cemetery, a place full of טומאת מת
Lingering, staying in a place for a set amount of time
Lashes, the punishment for breaking a לא תעשה

phrases.english: Rava asks:
A nazir who is in a cemetery, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means someone who takes the vow while already standing in the cemetery, not someone who walks in later.

phrases.english: Does he need to linger there to get lashes,
or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that a טמא שנזר gets lashes. Now it asks when exactly that punishment applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a נזיר who took his vow in a cemetery must linger there before he becomes liable for מלקות.

steps.title: What case is רבא asking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation רבא's question could actually apply to.
steps.whatsHappening: Before trying to answer, the גמרא asks what exact situation רבא means. This line sets up the next move, where the גמרא tests one possible case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A question only makes sense if there is a real case where the answer could go either way. The גמרא wants to find a case where lingering could actually matter.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What situation are we talking about?

phrases.english: What is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact setting of רבא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific circumstances in which רבא's question about lingering would make sense.

steps.title: If he was warned, lingering makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: Suppose they warned him not to take the vow. Then he should get lashes right away, just like a נזיר who is warned not to enter a cemetery. So lingering would not be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose they told him, "Do not become a נזיר." Then why would lingering be needed? Why does a נזיר who enters a cemetery not need to linger? Because they warn him. Here too they warn him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out the first possible case, where people warned him not to take the vow in the cemetery. It shows that in this case the question falls apart, because the warning alone makes him liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר who walks into a cemetery gets lashes without lingering, because he was given a התראה before he broke the rule. A person warned 'don't make the vow here' who goes ahead and vows is the same. So רבא cannot be asking about this case, and the גמרא will need a different one.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, used to test one possible explanation
Do not become a נזיר (the warning)
Why do I need it?
They warn him. This is התראה, the warning needed before lashes.
Here too

steps.confusionAlert: The comparison here is to a נזיר who walks INTO a cemetery. It is not the case of someone who becomes טמא in the מקדש. The walking-in נזיר is punished right away because he was warned.

phrases.english: If you say that they told him
"Do not become a nazir,"
why do I need lingering?
A nazir, what is the reason
phrases.notes: This is a regular נזיר who walks into a cemetery.

phrases.english: that he does not need lingering?
Because they warn him.
Here too they warn him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible case for רבא's question and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבא's question is about a person who was warned not to take the vow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A נזיר who enters a cemetery needs no lingering because he was warned. A warned person who vows in a cemetery is the same, so there is nothing left to ask.
